newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FARM MINISTER'S DISMISSAL STILL UNDECIDED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FARM MINISTER'S DISMISSAL STILL UNDECIDED.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and chiefs of the co-ruling Peasant Party failed to discuss the proposed dismissal of the farm minister on Tuesday, because they could not agree on where to meet.
The minister, Roman Jagielinski, told a news briefing that he and Cimoszewicz had been waiting at the government headquarters building but the Peasant leaders had not shown up.
"Prime Minister Cimoszewicz, the host in this building, has been waiting for the meeting here," Jagielinski told a news briefing.
The Peasants, holding a meeting of their executive body, were meanwhile awaiting the prime minister in their headquarters some four kilometres away.

Last week, Peasants leaders demanded that Cimoszewicz dismiss Jagielinski, their party colleague, alleging that he had pursued mistaken farm policies which brought a $1 billion deficit in food trade last year.
The argument over Jagielinski is the latest row to rattle the uneasy three-year-old coalition of the Peasants and Cimoszewicz's larger ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance.
Cimoszewicz, who strongly defends Jagielinski's record, has said that before deciding on whether to sack the minister, he needed more details on the Peasant leaders' request.
No government official would comment on Tuesday on when Cimoszewicz might be planning to decide the minister's fate.

Jagielinski repeated that he disagreed with the allegations and said he would not quit unless dismissed by the prime minister. He suggested the demand to oust him was a gesture by the Peasant party in campaigning for parliamentary elections later this year.
Analysts say that the departure of Jagielinski, one of Peasants' most liberal politicians, might improve their rating among Poland's numerous small, often poor farmers who seek government subsidies.
Jagielinski also made clear he thought the motion to fire him was an act of revenge by Peasant party president Waldemar Pawlak, whose leadership Jagielinski challenged last year.

Pawlak said there would be no formal meeting between the two coalition parties until Cimoszewicz dismissed Jagielinski, whose post is up to the Peasants to fill under terms of their agreement. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
